items.prompt: Which word is the correct short form of "do not"?

options.why: The apostrophe goes where the letter o is missing, not at the end.
The apostrophe must sit in the place of the missing o, which is after the n.
The apostrophe is in the wrong place, so the word looks odd.

hints: Which letter disappears when the two words join?
The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter.
Join do and not, then take out the o from not.
items.explanation: In "do not" the o of not is missing, so we write don't. The apostrophe sits where the o was.

items.prompt: Write the short form of "she is" using an apostrophe.
hints: Two words become one word.
The apostrophe replaces a missing letter.
Which letter does is lose?
items.explanation: She is becomes she's. The apostrophe takes the place of the letter i.

items.prompt: One dog owns the bowl. Which sentence is correct?

options.why: Without an apostrophe it is not clear that the bowl belongs to the dog.
This shows more than one dog owns the bowl.

options.text: The dog is bowl was empty.
options.why: The words are not joined into a possessive form.

hints: Who owns the bowl, one dog or many?
For one owner, add an apostrophe and s.
Write the owner, then add 's.
items.explanation: For a single owner we add an apostrophe and s: the dog's bowl.

items.prompt: ___ a shame that the old tree has lost ___ leaves.
hints: One gap means "it is". The other shows belonging.
Try saying "it is" in each gap.
Its with no apostrophe shows that something belongs to it.
items.explanation: It's is short for it is. Its with no apostrophe means belonging to it, like his or her.

hints: Find the name of the owner.
The apostrophe goes between the name and the s.
Start with the word That.
items.explanation: Kofi owns the football, so we write Kofi's with an apostrophe and s.

items.prompt: The bags belong to two girls. Which phrase is correct?

options.why: This shows only one girl.
The apostrophe is missing, so belonging is not shown.
The plural girls already ends in s, so an extra s is not added.

hints: How many owners are there?
For a plural noun that ends in s, add the apostrophe after the s.
Write girls first, then think about where the apostrophe goes.
items.explanation: The plural girls already ends in s, so we only add an apostrophe after it: the girls' bags.

items.prompt: Sort the words by what the apostrophe does.
hints: Ask yourself: does it show who owns something?
Short forms like can't join two words and leave out letters.
Try replacing the phrase with two full words.
items.explanation: Wulan's bike, the teacher's desk and the children's toys show who owns something. Can't, we've and they'd have missing letters.

items.prompt: Fix the mistake. The childrens toys were all over the floor. Write the correct form of childrens, with its apostrophe.
hints: The toys belong to the children.
Children is a plural that does not end in s.
For irregular plurals like this, add apostrophe and s.
items.explanation: Children is an irregular plural that does not end in s, so we add 's: children's toys.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses its or it's correctly?

options.why: It's means it is, so this does not make sense.
Its with no apostrophe cannot mean it is.

options.text: I think it's time to go home.

options.why: Belonging uses its, with no apostrophe.

hints: Try replacing the word with "it is".
If "it is" fits, you need the apostrophe.
Read each sentence with "it is" in the gap.
items.explanation: It's means it is. In "it is time to go home" the short form works, so it's is right.

head: Two words
Short form
hints: Look at which letters are left out.
Join the two words and put the apostrophe where letters vanish.
Start with they are: which letter does are lose?
items.explanation: They are becomes they're, would not becomes wouldn't, and it has becomes it's.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences with correct apostrophes.

options.text: The babies' cots are in the next room.
The men's team won the match.
We saw three bird's in the tree.
options.why: Plural birds does not need an apostrophe, because nothing belongs to it.
Its been means it has been, so it needs it's.

hints: Check each sentence for an owner or missing letters.
Plural nouns not ending in s take 's. Plural nouns ending in s take s'.
Ask: is there a real owner or a missing letter?
items.explanation: The babies' cots and the men's team show belonging correctly, and James's hat is also fine. The other two sentences use apostrophes incorrectly.

items.prompt: In which sentence does the apostrophe show missing letters, not belonging?

options.why: Here the apostrophe shows that the car belongs to Mum.
Here the apostrophe shows that the coach belongs to the team.
Here the apostrophe shows that the field belongs to the farmers.

hints: Try swapping the word with "is" or "has".
If the short form can be written out as two words, letters are missing.
Test: could "Mum's" be "Mum has"?
items.explanation: "Mum's gone" means "Mum has gone", so the apostrophe stands for missing letters. The other three show who owns something.

items.prompt: Citra read a sign at the school gate. It said: "Please leave your bikes' by the wall. Its not allowed to block the gate." She wanted to fix the two mistakes.

parts.prompt: Which word wrongly has an apostrophe?

options.why: No apostrophe belongs in this word.
This word is fine as it is.
This word is fine as it is.

parts.prompt: Write the correct form of "Its" at the start of the second sentence.

hints: Look for a plural noun that is not an owner.
Read the second sentence with "it is" in it.
A plain plural does not need an apostrophe.
items.explanation: Bikes is a plain plural, so it needs no apostrophe. "It is not allowed" needs the short form It's.

items.prompt: The hats belong to all the pupils in the class. Complete the phrase: the ___ hats.
hints: There is more than one owner.
The plural pupils already ends in s.
Add only the apostrophe.
items.explanation: The plural pupils ends in s, so we add an apostrophe after it: the pupils' hats.
